races.name: JCB Mini-Exacavator Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Born A Rebel
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who ran creditably at 7f on good recently; Aroon D'Arcy claims 7lb off a mark of 66 which gives the combination a live chance if the closing fractions are fast enough, though stepping back to 1m from shorter trips is worth noting.|

runners_data.name: Into Combat
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's runner returns after a 248-day absence — significant layoff to flag — and while Prescott handlers often target horses fresh, Into Combat's form shows a repeated pattern of fading in the finish; a true hold-up type pushed onto the map in midfield, but the long break makes it hard to rely on.|

runners_data.name: Gladiadora
runners_data.note: The only confirmed prominent-style runner apart from Valentine Boy, and her record shows a win and three places from 15 runs on similar ground including a recent second on good; the tongue-tie is retained and Liam Wright's claim could be decisive if she can sit second and pounce.|

runners_data.name: Timely Affair
runners_data.note: Recent form is strong — placed or winning in four of last five over 7-8f on standard/good — and although a genuine hold-up type forced into a midfield mapping, she is versatile enough to track the pace; the hood suggests a horse that needs covering up, and William Knight's yard is firing (3/19 in 14 days).|

runners_data.name: Siam Fox
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 8f on good ground and carries the tongue-tie and blinkers combination that clearly suits; at OR 61 off a mark that looks achievable, but a true hold-up horse whose style fit is discounted here by redistribution — traffic management at this course will be key.|

runners_data.name: Atlantic Sunset
runners_data.note: All recent form is at 11-16f, making this 8f trip a significant drop in distance; a hold-up runner who seems better suited to staying trips, and the step down to a flat mile at Newmarket against quicker opponents looks tough.|

runners_data.name: Pay Attention
runners_data.note: Placed on good ground over 8f recently and her trainer Faye Bramley has had a productive 14-day spell (3/8); a natural hold-up runner whose last win came at this trip on good, with the visor retained — she is one of the more credible closers if she can find daylight.|

runners_data.name: King Of Charm
runners_data.note: Second last time out over 8f on good and the hood is fitted, but a true hold-up type who has struggled on turf in recent starts (no win in 15 outings); Alice Bond's 5lb claim helps, yet the style fit discount means this horse would need everything to go right.|

runners_data.name: Freddie's Star
runners_data.note: Top-rated horse in the field at OR 70, but recent form on good ground is poor (11th at 8f last time on good, 0 wins on this going from 7 runs); the hood is fitted and Roger Teal's yard has hit form (2/16 in 14 days), but a hold-up style on a flat track with a controlled pace makes his task difficult.|

runners_data.name: Valentine Boy
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and key pace-setter for the entire race; holds the hood and has won twice over 8f on standard ground, but has not won on good-to-firm and his STYLE_FIT tag signals he is a horse who naturally prefers to be ridden with cover — watch whether Jude Fernandes commits or tries to drop him in.|

runners_data.name: Didaar
runners_data.note: Returns after 142 days off — the longest break in the field — and while Gihan Arnolda's yard has been modestly active, the layoff combined with a hold-up style on a track and trip that rewards position makes this hard to fancy at a price; best form came at shorter on standard ground.|

races.paceDynamic: Valentine Boy is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with Gladiadora the only other prominent-style horse, he should face minimal early pressure and be allowed to dictate from the front at a sustainable gallop on good-to-firm ground over Newmarket's flat July mile. With one horse setting the fractions unchallenged, the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to string the field out, meaning the race will be run at a controlled tempo before a sprint-style finish up the straight. The field is heavily skewed toward hold-up types — Into Combat, Timely Affair, Siam Fox, Atlantic Sunset, Pay Attention and King Of Charm are all genuine closers redistributed into midfield on the map because there are simply too many true hold-up horses to show at the rear; of these, Timely Affair, Siam Fox and Pay Attention appear most likely to actually occupy tracking positions given their recent placing patterns. A steadily-run mile with one leader suits prominent racers and horses who can travel within easy reach of the pace, making Gladiadora and any horse capable of sitting close to Valentine Boy the primary beneficiaries of this race shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Valentine Boy Controls Unopposed
scenarios.trigger: If Valentine Boy leads from the gate and Gladiadora settles into second without applying pressure, creating a truly steady single-file gallop.
scenarios.body: If Valentine Boy leads from the gate and Gladiadora settles into second without applying pressure, creating a truly steady single-file gallop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Sprint Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just fast enough that Valentine Boy fades late and the race turns into a flat-out sprint from two furlongs out, favouring horses with a sharp late gear.
scenarios.body: If the pace is just fast enough that Valentine Boy fades late and the race turns into a flat-out sprint from two furlongs out, favouring horses with a sharp late gear.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is so slow that Valentine Boy ties up in the final furlong and Gladiadora swoops from a tracking position to capitalise.
scenarios.body: If the early gallop is so slow that Valentine Boy ties up in the final furlong and Gladiadora swoops from a tracking position to capitalise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: High Draw, Fast Ground Bias
scenarios.trigger: If good-to-firm conditions produce a pronounced track bias toward horses racing wide or high in the draw, shuffling the finishing order unexpectedly.
scenarios.body: If good-to-firm conditions produce a pronounced track bias toward horses racing wide or high in the draw, shuffling the finishing order unexpectedly.

watchPoints.text: Valentine Boy's jockey Jude Fernandes (7lb claimer) has never ridden a confirmed front-runner in a compressed field of hold-up types — watch whether he commits to the lead from the gate or allows another horse to set the pace, which would fundamentally alter the entire race shape.

Into Combat's 248-day absence is the red flag of the race; Sir Mark Prescott is a master with returning horses but Into Combat has a confirmed pattern of fading in the finish, and if it jumps fresh and leads the early pace, the race could be set up falsely for closers.

Atlantic Sunset's trip profile is a serious concern — all five recent runs have been at 11-16f and this 8f flat contest is a sharp drop in distance; if she struggles for early pace she will be tailed off before the field reaches the two-furlong pole.

Timely Affair is fitted with a hood (headgear flagged) and has been placed in four of her last five, but her trainer William Knight has a strong 14-day record (3/19) — monitor market moves, as any support here likely reflects yard confidence over an obvious form concern.

Freddie's Star is top-rated but has recorded zero wins from seven starts on good going; if the ground is riding genuinely good-to-firm as the going report confirms, his class advantage on ratings may be neutralised by his going preference, opening the door for lower-rated rivals.

races.name: JCB British EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
JCB Fastrac EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
JCB Hydrogen Handicap

runners_data.name: Valley Ofthe Kings
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Dylan Cunha though the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) tempers confidence — recent form shows finishes of 9th and 7th, simulated-going record is moderate (0W3P on Good-type), and 73 days off adds a fitness question despite the tactical advantage of likely leading.|

runners_data.name: Expert Agent
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams runner in excellent recent form (1-2-1 in last three, both wins over 6f on Good ground) for Jack Callan; best profile in the field for this pace shape, prominent style perfectly suited, and 35 days off is no concern given that consistency.|

runners_data.name: Twilight Fun
runners_data.note: A prominent runner in headgear for Chelsea Banham whose simulated-going record (0W0P from 3 on Good-type) undermines claims despite front-running tendencies; finished 14th at Haydock last time on Soft, and no wins on Good ground in recent history is a real flag.|

runners_data.name: Sapphire Steps
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon sends this 3yo hold-up filly who has competed exclusively on Good ground (6/6 in similar conditions, 1W1P) — she is a genuine closer and won't be inconvenienced by style redistribution around her, but needs the pace to genuinely stack up.|

runners_data.name: Bintola
runners_data.note: Harry Charlton's 3yo won last time over 6f on Good ground for Zac Lloyd and races prominently — recent course and distance form (1/6f/GOO) is the most directly relevant of any runner, making him a compelling prominent type if he gets a clean position.|

runners_data.name: Dutch Finale
runners_data.note: 282 days off is a significant fitness concern for this Stuart Williams hold-up type; has form on Good going over 6f (3/6f/GOO) but the layoff means any return to peak condition is speculative and the run is likely needed before he fires.|

runners_data.name: Goldwork
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's 3yo is a true prominent racer in headgear but has been displaced to midfield on the map — the field is too front-heavy for him to get his natural berth, and recent form reads 0-0-3-5-0, making the style friction an additional rather than standalone concern.|

runners_data.name: Sea Cookie
runners_data.note: Tom Clover's unexposed 3yo has a tidy profile (1-2-2 in last three, including a win over 6f on Good) and is a natural prominent type who in reality may struggle to secure that position in this competitive front-running field — if he can get close to the pace, the raw form is live.|

runners_data.name: Romantic Twilight
runners_data.note: William Stone's hold-up 3yo has won over 6f on Good ground at Newmarket (1/6f/GOO) and is genuine for the style, but a finishing position of 13th last time on Good at this course is an immediate concern that form needs explaining before backing.|

races.paceDynamic: Valley Ofthe Kings is the confirmed front-runner here, likely to stride into a clear lead from the outset on Newmarket's July Course straight six, setting a sustainable gallop that plays to his preference for racing prominently. Expert Agent, Twilight Fun, and Bintola are all natural prominent types who will press for early position, meaning the lead will not go uncontested — Valley Ofthe Kings faces genuine early competition that could stretch the tempo and string the field out. This field carries more prominent runners than the race shape can accommodate: Goldwork and Sea Cookie are both true front-running or prominent types that have been displaced to midfield on the map, with Expert Agent and Bintola most likely to physically secure the prominent positions behind any leader given their proven recent form on Good ground. A strongly-run pace-contested six furlongs at Newmarket, with multiple horses fighting for the front rank, strongly favours horses who can race prominently with cover or hold a handy position in the first half and sustain their effort to the line — the profile most suited here is the prominent horse with Good-ground form who travels within themselves and doesn't have to expend energy scrapping for position.

scenarios.title: Prominent Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Valley Ofthe Kings dictates from the front and the contested early pace burns off the hold-up types before the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Valley Ofthe Kings dictates from the front and the contested early pace burns off the hold-up types before the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closer Delivers Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace genuinely overheats with multiple prominent types fighting hard, creating a fast-run race that exposes the front rank in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If the pace genuinely overheats with multiple prominent types fighting hard, creating a fast-run race that exposes the front rank in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Midway
scenarios.trigger: If Valley Ofthe Kings fails to sustain the gallop after a contested early break, causing the pace to flatline in the middle of the race.
scenarios.body: If Valley Ofthe Kings fails to sustain the gallop after a contested early break, causing the pace to flatline in the middle of the race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the race fragments into small groups and a hold-up runner finds a clear run through at the two-furlong pole while the prominent battle cancels itself out.
scenarios.body: If the race fragments into small groups and a hold-up runner finds a clear run through at the two-furlong pole while the prominent battle cancels itself out.

watchPoints.text: Watch Valley Ofthe Kings in the opening furlong — if Expert Agent, Twilight Fun, and Bintola all press hard for the lead, the pace could be significantly faster than a lone front-runner scenario and any horse unable to relax prominently will be in trouble by halfway.

Sea Cookie and Goldwork are both natural prominent types forced wider in the field on the map — observe their pre-race odds movement as a market signal for whether connections believe they can secure their preferred position from the draw.

Dutch Finale's 282-day absence warrants monitoring in the parade ring and early market moves; if the horse shows any signs of fitness concern in the paddock, the layoff risk becomes a live danger to any scenario that relies on him firing fresh.

Sapphire Steps has raced exclusively on Good or Good-to-Firm ground throughout her career — the confirmed Good-to-Firm going report for this race slot is directly aligned with her entire profile, making going conditions a genuine positive rather than a neutral factor.|

Bintola's win last time came over exactly this course-distance-going combination (1/6f/GOO); at OR 81 off a mark set by that performance, watch whether the handicapper has left enough lenience or whether he's been priced to reflect it already.|

races.name: JCB Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Dojin
runners_data.note: Comes in on the back of back-to-back wins at 11-12f on Fibresand (Southwell), now asked to front up on turf over 1m6f for the first time — the step to turf is a genuine unknown, but the style fit at the head of affairs here is natural and Robert Havlin's booking for Stuart Woods adds confidence; 47 days since last run is worth monitoring but not alarming.|

runners_data.name: Kuredu King
runners_data.note: Donald McCain's gelding has placed twice at 16-17f on good at Chelmsford and Chester, giving him course-relevant stamina credentials, but his recent form includes an eighth at 16f; the blinkers-headgear flag (hg:b) suggests connections are looking for sharper focus, and Dougie Costello is an upgrade.|

runners_data.name: Sixpack
runners_data.note: James Owen's progressive performer arrives with the freshest legs in the race (9 days) and holds wins at 12-14f on both soft and good; the hood (hg:p) is retained and his record of 2W5P in similar going conditions suggests he handles this surface well — Zac Lloyd takes the ride and the OR drop to 81 after a recent third keeps him competitive.|

runners_data.name: Youthful King
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old hold-up performer whose recent form (four consecutive beaten runs at 10-14f) gives little encouragement for a handicap off OR 79; the 7lb claim from Jude Fernandes marginally offsets the weight burden, but the horse's sim-going strike rate (1W3P at 1m5f+ on good) does little to inspire confidence against this pace setup.|

runners_data.name: Roadlesstravelled
runners_data.note: Jonjo & A J O'Neill's seven-year-old has solid placed form at 11-12f on Fibresand and won off a comparable mark, but returns here after 87 days off — the most significant layoff in the field; a natural prominent runner who cannot realistically get that berth in this company, meaning Alistair Rawlinson will likely have to settle for a deeper position than the horse prefers, which dims its chance.|

races.paceDynamic: Dojin is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of just five and will set a measured, sustainable gallop over this 1m6f trip on good-to-firm ground at Newmarket's July course — a flat track that typically rewards those able to control proceedings from the front. Sixpack will press for a prominent position alongside Dojin, and with Roadlesstravelled also a natural prominent type (redistributed to midfield given the competition for that real estate), there is a modest degree of early positional pressure but nothing that should genuinely destabilise the pace. Kuredu King and Youthful King will track from the rear, relying on the pace being strong enough to close into, though in a small, unhurried field that is far from guaranteed. The field holds more prominent types than can all secure their natural berths — Dojin and Sixpack are best-placed to actually dictate, while Roadlesstravelled is unlikely to get the prominent pitch it prefers. This race shape decisively favours prominent runners who can dictate or sit just off a gentle pace, making a strong staying effort from close to the front the most likely winning formula.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dojin Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Dojin leads without serious pressure and sets a comfortable, even tempo that suits a stamina-based finish.
scenarios.body: If Dojin leads without serious pressure and sets a comfortable, even tempo that suits a stamina-based finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Dojin sets an honest pace and Sixpack or Roadlesstravelled tracks closely enough to challenge in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If Dojin sets an honest pace and Sixpack or Roadlesstravelled tracks closely enough to challenge in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Strikes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong early and creates enough of a test to bring the hold-up horses into contention in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely strong early and creates enough of a test to bring the hold-up horses into contention in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos Unpicks Field
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses contest the early lead aggressively, causing an irregular pace pattern that scrambles the expected finishing order.
scenarios.body: If multiple horses contest the early lead aggressively, causing an irregular pace pattern that scrambles the expected finishing order.

watchPoints.text: Dojin leads a field of five with no genuine pace rival — if it quickens off a false, slow gallop in the final quarter-mile, hold-up horses Kuredu King and Youthful King may simply have too much ground to make up.
Sixpack arrives just 9 days after its last run and with the hood retained; if the hood fails to sharpen the horse's focus early, it may miss the break and lose its prominent pitch to Dojin unopposed.

Roadlesstravelled has been off the track for 87 days — the longest absence in the race — and if ring rust shows in the early stages the horse will fail to secure even the midfield position it has been mapped to, making its chance effectively nil.

Kuredu King is equipped with blinkers for the first time or re-applied (hg:b flag) — watch the pre-race market move; if connections expect a significant behavioural improvement, a stronger market move than expected would be a meaningful signal in a race this small.

With only five runners and a flat, undemanding course, the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to genuinely test stamina — runners racing prominently are structurally advantaged, and any drift in the market for Dojin or Sixpack should be treated seriously before post time.

races.name: JCB Hydradig Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Ventana
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up filly for Charles Hills who has placed over 6f on good ground (2nd last time out), but the modest three-run form string (8-52) and Zac Lloyd in the saddle leaves questions; Newmarket's July Course demands early tactical awareness she may lack from the back.|

runners_data.name: Artista
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster's filly has run predominantly over 5f and is stepping up to 6f for the first time in her recent campaign — she is a hold-up type whose 5f form (1W3P on similar going) may not fully translate to this extra furlong in a sprint-finish scenario.|

runners_data.name: Zoustar Dreams
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins including a 6f success on good ground gives her the most compelling recent trajectory in the field; the visor stays on, Ed Dunlop's yard is hitting a decent strike rate (T14: 2/20), and Jack Callan's 3lb claim is a tangible asset — she's racing in a role that suits her.|

runners_data.name: Nifty
runners_data.note: A genuine deep hold-up filly whose redistribution to midfield reflects that she simply cannot get to the back of this field — Richard Hughes has her ready (T14: 2/40) and she showed a placed effort at 6f on good ground, but racing ahead of her natural position tempers her chance in a compressed sprint.|

runners_data.name: Bluebluelectricblu
runners_data.note: Tom Dascombe's filly has been a model of consistency in placing without winning (4-4-6-4-8 recent form) and is one of the fillies whose naturally rear-of-field style has been pushed forward on the map — her wider-trip form over 7f on soft suggests this 6f on good ground is less ideal, and style displacement is a double constraint.|

runners_data.name: Mortubo
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on good ground on her most recent start — the standout relevant form in the field — and Gary & Josh Moore's yard is in serious form (T14: 4/34); the tongue-tie stays on and she has 6f good-ground winning experience to call upon, though like all in this race she can't get the natural hold-up position she'd prefer.|

runners_data.name: Startled Lady
runners_data.note: William Knight's filly has a solid record of placing without winning (0W2P on similar going, 2nd and 3rd in recent outings) and is tactically adept enough to take a prominent position when required; 16 days since last run, Neil Callan experienced enough to find daylight in a sprint, but the absence of a win is a persistent concern.|

runners_data.name: Spacewoman
runners_data.note: Henry Candy's filly drops significantly in class (OR 60) and has headgear on (p-hood), placed twice over 6f on similar ground — her best form came over 6f at standside tracks and she's one of the smaller weights here at 125lbs; her natural rear-of-field tendency is accommodated on the map only partially, and Nicola Currie will need a clean run.|

runners_data.name: Reality Queen
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's filly has been off 112 days — the longest layoff in the field — which is a significant red flag, though she won over 6f on good ground on her most recent winning start (sim-going: 1W1P); that fresh bounce could cut either way and Robert Havlin's experience won't compensate for a lack of recent fitness evidence.|

races.paceDynamic: With every runner in this nine-filly field carrying a hold-up profile and no confirmed front-runner declared, the early pace is likely to be pedestrian at best, creating an ugly dawdling sprint rather than a true-run 6f on the July Course. The entire field maps as hold-up types, meaning several runners will be forced against their grain and must settle closer to the pace than they would prefer — Nifty, Mortubo, Bluebluelectricblu, Startled Lady, Spacewoman, and Reality Queen are all genuine hold-up fillies who will find themselves pushed into unfamiliar midfield slots simply because the rear is overcrowded. The resulting shape will likely see a slow early gallop and a compressed field hitting the Bunbury Mile junction before exploding into a flat-out 2f dash, with minimal advantage gained by position early. This race shape heavily favours whichever filly has the most raw finishing speed in a sprint, and those with the clearest run from a decent draw and the sharpest recent form over 6f on good ground will have a meaningful edge over those who need a true pace to showcase their hold-up ability.

watchPoints.text: Mortubo and Zoustar Dreams both carry winning form over 6f on good ground — if either secures clean daylight in the final furlong scramble, they have the profile to dominate this shape.|

Reality Queen's 112-day absence is the longest in the field by a wide margin — watch the market for any significant support or drift as a proxy for stable confidence, as the form means little without fitness.|

With nine hold-up fillies and no genuine front-runner, watch the early stages carefully — if the pace collapses entirely, the race becomes a lottery and draw position (particularly low-numbered stalls for a straight course) could be disproportionately influential.|
Artista has not run beyond 5f in recent starts and steps up to 6f here — worth monitoring whether she gets competitive in the second half of the race or fades once the fractions stretch.|

The Moore yard (Mortubo, T14: 4/34) and Dascombe yard (Bluebluelectricblu, T14: 1/11) are at opposite ends of their current form cycles — trainer momentum is a legitimate secondary factor in a race where the pace shape alone cannot separate the field.|

races.name: JCB Tele-Handler Handicap

runners_data.name: Diomed Duke
runners_data.note: Sole genuine front-runner in the race; Stuart Williams' four-year-old carries 140lbs but has a strong style-fit for this Newmarket five-furlong configuration on good ground, and with no credible challenger for the lead his ability to dictate terms is the defining factor in how this race unfolds.

runners_data.name: Good Earth
runners_data.note: Michael Herrington's nine-year-old has won twice at six furlongs on good ground recently including an impressive course win, and returns on just eight days' rest in good form; a hold-up operator who needs something to aim at, and the controlled pace Diomed Duke is likely to set could blunt his finishing thrust.

runners_data.name: Tuscan Point
runners_data.note: Adam Kirby's four-year-old has claims at five furlongs in good-to-firm conditions with a solid sim-going profile of 8/15, and the addition of eye-shields (hg: et) is worth noting; a hold-up horse who will be ridden with patience by apprentice Ryan Kavanagh, and needs the pace to lift in the final two furlongs.

runners_data.name: Shavkat
runners_data.note: The second prominent-type in the field, Hilal Kobeissi's four-year-old wore a tongue-tie (hg: tp) and returns after 33 days off with a modest handicap record on similar going; if Finley Marsh elects to push forward, Shavkat becomes the only realistic source of pressure on Diomed Duke but has little to recommend that aggression on form.

runners_data.name: Coyy
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's three-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse by style — winning twice from five on good ground — but is redistributed into midfield here because the field is heavy with rearward-runners all competing for the same space; the style-fit flag (0.92) is an honest reflection that Coyy is unlikely to get the clean, late-running scenario it requires, which tempers its appeal despite solid recent form.

runners_data.name: Court Drive
runners_data.note: Gay Kelleway's five-year-old won on soft ground at six furlongs but has a deeply unimpressive record on all-weather and standard surfaces (1/15 on sim-going); a natural hold-up horse pushed into a midfield mapping position because of field congestion at the rear, and both the redistribution and the going profile reduce confidence materially.

runners_data.name: Quantum Power
runners_data.note: Tom Clover's three-year-old is a prominent-type who has placed at five and six furlongs on good ground, with the visor (hg: v) retained; Jack Callan takes a 3lb claim and the horse is at its best in a steadily-run race where it can sit just off the pace and pounce, making it the most interesting secondary threat to any leader who gets first run.

races.paceDynamic: Diomed Duke is the sole confirmed front-runner in a seven-horse field and, with only Shavkat as a second prominent-type to apply any pressure, is highly likely to take up the lead unchallenged from the gates over this sharp Newmarket five furlongs on good-to-firm ground. The pace will therefore be sustainable rather than frantic — a controlled, metronomic gallop that keeps the field strung out and denies hold-up horses the fast sectionals they need to close late. Coyy and Court Drive are genuine hold-up horses but are mapped into midfield here because the field holds more come-from-behind types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear, meaning neither is likely to operate in their true zone. This race shape — an uncontested leader setting honest but not scorching fractions — strongly favours prominent racers and front-runners who can exploit the clean passage and the rising ground into the Bunbury Mile junction, with true hold-up horses disadvantaged by the absence of a pace collapse to reel in.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Handicap Chaos; No Clear Winner
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses break poorly, traffic problems materialise across the track, or the pace proves much faster than anticipated.
scenarios.body: If multiple horses break poorly, traffic problems materialise across the track, or the pace proves much faster than anticipated.

watchPoints.text: Diomed Duke's barrier draw and early reaction — if he breaks cleanly and hits the front within the first furlong, the race is set in his favour; any stumble or slow start immediately opens up the race for Shavkat and the prominent brigade.

Shavkat's early intentions under Finley Marsh — if the horse is pushed forward aggressively to test Diomed Duke, the tempo lifts sharply and the entire race shape shifts from controlled lead to contested pace, materially improving Quantum Power's chances.

Good Earth's finishing position entering the final two furlongs — Michael Herrington's nine-year-old has the form to be competitive but needs to be travelling strongly by the two-furlong pole; if still well held at that point, the controlled pace has beaten him.

Coyy and Court Drive racing positions at the break — both are genuinely rearward-pattern horses competing for the same physical space, and if both are forced wider or further back than ideal, neither is likely to produce the decisive late burst their true style demands.

Quantum Power's headgear (visor) and response to the good-to-firm ground — the horse has form on the surface but the visor is the key variable; if it produces its best jumping quality and Jack Callan can slot in third or fourth early, it is the horse most likely to benefit from any lead collapse in the final furlong.
